title: What Are You Doing Now?
summary: Learn how to talk about actions happening right now. Use the present continuous to describe life at this exact moment.

sections.p: We use the present continuous to talk about things happening right now. We use the verb 'to be' (am, is, are) plus an action word ending in '-ing'. For example, instead of just saying 'I read', we say 'I am reading' if the book is open in front of us at this exact moment.

ex.mean: food is in my mouth right this second
music is playing in her ears now

sections.p: When talking about yourself, use 'am' plus the '-ing' verb. For one other person or thing like he, she, or it, use 'is' plus the '-ing' verb. These are great for describing what people around you are doing right this second.

ex.en: I am working at my desk.
ex.mean: I am doing my job right now

ex.en: He is running in the park.
ex.mean: his feet are moving fast outside now

sections.p: When talking about groups or the person you are talking to, use 'are' plus the '-ing' verb. This helps you describe group activities and things happening all around you in real time.

ex.mean: we are studying this lesson now
those people are kicking a ball now

tip: Look around your room right now and make three sentences. Say out loud what you are doing, what a friend is doing, and what you both are wearing!

quiz.en: I ___ reading a very good book.
She ___ cooking dinner in the kitchen.
Which sentence means it is happening now?
